models.title: Collinear acoustic Doppler frequency on the forward-crossing branch
models.summary: Corrects b01 collinear-acoustic-doppler@r1: removes an unnecessarily subsonic observer upper bound and admits the explicitly labeled zero-crossing-rate limit. Source remains subsonic, and the same canonical relationship/ID and medium-frame sign mapping are retained. No new coverage is counted for this revision.

relationship.original_equation: f_o = f_s (v +/- v_o)/(v -/+ v_s), top signs for approach
relationship.locator: University Physics 1 Eq. 17.20 and Table 17.4; subsonic derivation preceding Eq. 17.18; Example 17.8
relationship.translation_notes: Introduce signed u_s=+v_s for source approach and -v_s for recession, and u_o=+v_o for observer approach and -v_o for recession, all relative to the medium. Source Eq. 17.19 follows from lambda=(v+u_o)*T_o on the approach branch: positive approach has no u_o<v requirement. Source's subsonic-source restriction stays -v<u_s<v with nonzero v-u_s. r1 imposed an unnecessary symmetric subsonic observer profile; r2 uses u_o>=-v to retain nonnegative crossing orientation, with no upper observer speed bound except classical/passive-probe applicability. At u_o=-v the observed phase is static: f_o=0 is an admitted zero-crossing-rate limit, with no finite observed period. Negative crossing orientation u_o<-v would need a separate qualified magnitude/branch treatment, not negative heard frequency. Hz*(m/s)/(m/s)=Hz; no unit scales or physical constants inlined. Relativistic light Doppler is not this law.

variables.definition: Acoustic cycles emitted per unit time by the source under classical common time in the medium frame.
variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and ideal passive observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure and constant prescribed collinear endpoint velocities. Source is subsonic. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s. Forward-crossing branch u_o>=-v; u_o=-v is the zero-crossing-rate limit. Source/observer ordering remains unchanged over the modeled interval.

variables.definition: Nonnegative rate of acoustic phase crossings at the observer on the declared branch; zero denotes a wave-comoving static phase pattern, not a zero emitted carrier frequency.
variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and ideal passive observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure and constant prescribed collinear endpoint velocities. Source is subsonic. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s. Forward-crossing branch u_o>=-v; u_o=-v is the zero-crossing-rate limit. Source/observer ordering remains unchanged over the modeled interval.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative. Positive for u_o>-v; zero at u_o=-v as an explicitly admitted limiting identity. Shift f_o-f_s may be positive, negative or zero.

assumptions: Source assumption: constant source frequency, homogeneous acoustic medium at rest, and collinear endpoint velocities in that same medium frame; no source/observer crossing in the chosen interval.
Source restriction: source speed is subsonic (-v<u_s<v), so emitted forward wavefronts remain ordered and v-u_s>0.
Application branch: observer u_o>=-v gives nonnegative forward phase-crossing rate; equality is an explicitly admitted static-phase/zero-arrival-rate limit, not a repeating observed oscillation.

Kinematic idealization: observer is a passive probe of the prescribed acoustic field; self-generated disturbances/wakes are not computed. Observer approaching faster than sound is not rejected solely by an unsupported symmetric speed guard.
Source scope: classical acoustics, common time coordinate, no relativistic electromagnetic Doppler or noncollinear geometry.
limitations: For u_o=-v, no successive phase arrivals occur; a finite observed period or arrival-spacing inverse is unavailable even though the limiting crossing rate is zero.

For u_o<-v the oriented crossing rate changes sign; nonnegative physical-frequency magnitudes and their inverses need a separately evidenced branch/magnitude treatment. That branch is outside this record, not a claim that the motion is impossible.
Changing line-of-sight orientation, endpoint crossing, source supersonic/shock regimes or an observer's disturbance of the medium require more modeling.
No energy, intensity, loudness, audibility or perceptual-pitch relation is supplied; rounded textbook frequency examples are pedagogical arithmetic, not empirical calibration.

references.method: Published Example 17.8(a) gives 167 Hz (kept as expected, not replaced by 167.213...). Half the final integer-Hz reporting step is 0.5 Hz; the nominal rounded inputs yield an error about 0.213 Hz.

Published Example 17.8(a) gives 136 Hz after passage; keep this expected rather than recomputing 136 exactly for a different dataset. Nominal source data produce 136 Hz; tolerance 0.5 Hz follows integer reporting.

Limiting identity supported by Example 17.8(b): endpoints with equal laboratory velocity maintain their separation, so arrival intervals equal emission intervals. In this signed convention u_o=-u_s; f_o-f_s=0. A 1e-10 Hz tolerance only covers floating-point evaluation, not measurement precision.

Independent synthetic spacetime construction: source at x=0 moving +60 m/s, observer initially at x=30 m moving -20 m/s; waves travel +300 m/s. First front meets observer at 30/320=0.09375 s. Second emitted at 0.01 s from x=0.6 meets at t=0.10125 s by solving 0.6+300*(t-0.01)=30-20*t. Arrival spacing 0.0075 s yields 133 1/3 Hz. This constructs two events rather than substituting in the serialized frequency expression; tolerance covers repeating decimal arithmetic.

references.method: Independent synthetic wavefront events with source at x=0 moving +60 m/s, observer initially x=30 m moving -450 m/s, waves +300 m/s. First front meets at t=0.040 s. Second is emitted t=0.010 at x=0.6 and meets when 0.6+300*(t-0.01)=30-450*t, giving t=0.0432 s. Arrival spacing 0.0032 s means 312.5 Hz. The endpoints have not crossed before these events. This catches r1's overrestrictive u_o<v guard; decimal floating-point tolerance only.

references.method: Kinematic limiting identity: observer moves away at wave speed, so it stays at one phase of an already established train and sees no repeated phase crossings. It is not a case of two finite echo arrivals separated by zero time; observed period is unavailable. Expected zero follows constant-phase motion, independent of frequency-expression substitution. Numeric tolerance only.

rejection_cases.reason: At sonic source speed the forward wavefront spacing and denominator vanish; no finite ordinary Doppler frequency.
Observer velocity relative to the medium is not supplied; it must not be silently assumed zero.

Observer overtakes forward wavefronts in reverse order; the stated nonnegative forward-crossing branch is violated. Motion is physically possible but needs a separately qualified magnitude/branch model.

models.inverse_notes: Retain f_s>0,v>0,-v<u_s<v,u_o>=-v and the same classical medium-frame geometry. For f_s given f_o,v,u_s,u_o: f_s=f_o*(v-u_s)/(v+u_o), requiring u_o>-v and f_o>0; unique positive root. At u_o=-v,f_o=0 any positive f_s is compatible (underdetermined), while f_o>0 is inconsistent. For u_s given f_o,f_s,v,u_o: u_s=v-f_s*(v+u_o)/f_o, requiring f_o>0 and reconstructed -v<u_s<v; at f_o=0,u_o=-v every admissible u_s gives zero, so u_s is underdetermined. For u_o given f_o,f_s,v,u_s: u_o=f_o*(v-u_s)/f_s-v, requiring f_o>=0,f_s>0 and the reconstructed original guards; f_o=0 uniquely returns u_o=-v, no nonzero-f_o exclusion in this direction. For v given frequencies/velocities: v=(f_o*u_s+f_s*u_o)/(f_o-f_s), requiring f_o!=f_s, v>0,-v<u_s<v,u_o>=-v. If f_o=f_s then u_o=-u_s leaves all admissible v undetermined; otherwise inconsistent. Checks: f_o=312.5,f_s=100,v=300,u_o=450 -> u_s=60 and forward 312.5; inverse v=(312.5*60+100*450)/(312.5-100)=300. At f_o=0,f_s=100,u_s=60,u_o=-300 -> v=300; u_o inverse also gives -300. At zero endpoint motion, f_o=f_s=150, so shift is exactly zero with arbitrary admissible supplied v. Non-singular mentioned directions have one root; observed-frequency data alone do not establish causal identification.
